subject: Multi-year pricing request — price lock & renewal protections (QuantaPlane)
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Grant <ellis@quantaplane.com>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: 3-year pricing & options for renewal protections

Ellis — attaching the formal quote for your review (Redwood_Quote_QuantaPlane_20250512.pdf).

Recap: QuantaPlane asked for a multi-year option with a guaranteed price for the initial term and protections on renewal increases. Our standard multi-year offer is a 3-year commitment with an annual pricing uplift tied to an index (market band of 5–9%). Because you asked for hard caps and contractual renewal protection, I wanted to surface this to you and to our internal approvals path.

What we can offer today (terms in quote):
- 3-year fixed list price for year 1 (price lock)
- Annual uplift cap: up to 7% max per year (index-based adjustments capped)
- Renewal protection clause (proposed): Redwood will not increase list price for the first renewal by more than the uplift cap; any other material changes require 60 days' notice and mutual agreement.

These are non-standard compared to our template T&Cs — legal and deal desk approval required. If you like these guardrails, I will escalate for exec signoff and get a redline back.

Next steps: please confirm the uplift cap target (you listed 5%–8% in the call) and whether QuantaPlane can commit to a 3-year term and a minimum annual usage floor (helps offset the concession).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

—

Ava — thanks for the quick turnaround and the quote. A few clarifying items before I loop in procurement formally:

1) Uplift cap: We need a firm contractual cap not tied to a broad index — QuantaPlane wants a hard cap at renewal (we can accept up to 6% if needed).
2) Renewal protection: We want a clause that prevents unilateral price increases above the cap for at least the first renewal and a guarantee that any new product additions won't be mandatory to maintain the contracted pricing.
3) Term commitment: We are comfortable with 3 years but will want a limited exit right in year 2 for substantial breaches.

Procurement, please advise on what paperwork you need — and Ellis will share our standard contract playbook.

—

Ellis — appreciate the clarity. Quick answers and path forward: 

- Hard uplift cap: we can recommend 7% as our standard concession, but we can ask for an exception to 6% per your note — requires executive approval because it reduces our flexibility versus the index approach.
- Renewal protection: legal can add language that the first automatic renewal cannot exceed the agreed uplift cap and that any mandatory product changes that materially alter the deliverable must be mutually agreed.
- Exit right: we can include a limited material-breach exit in year 2 (standard carve — legal to confirm language).

I'm escalating to deal desk + finance (cc'd) for a formal multi-year approval. I am also attaching a proposed redline for internal review (QP_Contract_Redline_20250513.docx).

If markus or Rishi can confirm the uplift cap threshold they will approve, I'll send the updated contract to Ellis and procurement for signature.

Thanks — Ava

Markus / Laura — forwarding for approval. Highlights: potential 3-year commit with requested hard uplift cap (client asking for 6% max).

Impact summary: 
- ACV at proposed price lock (3yr) is $1.2M / year; reducing uplift cap from our index-based plan to a hard 6% reduces expected FY3 uplift by ~120k (conservative).
- Customer is strategic (AI platform vendor) with good expansion potential — upsell likelihood high after integrations.
- Legal redlines are minor; the main ask is the non-standard renewal protection and hard uplift cap.

Requested approvals: 
1) Executive approval for exception to pricing policy: allow 6% annual uplift cap for this deal.
2) Approval to include the renewal protection clause in the master services agreement.
3) If approved, authorize discount & revenue recognition treatment as noted in the attached spreadsheet (internal).

I recommend we make approval conditional on a minimum committed ARR (1.0M / year) and a signed PO within 30 days.

—Rishi

Team — after reviewing the revenue impact and strategic rationale, I will approve an exception with conditions.

Conditions for approval (must be in final SOW / contract):
- Uplift cap set to 6% (client request) — approved.
- Renewal protection: Redwood will not increase list price for the first renewal beyond the 6% cap; any other changes to fees require 60 days' notice and mutual consent.
- Minimum committed ARR: $1.0M per year across the 3-year term (to offset concession).
- Cancellation: 30 days' notice post-year-1 for material breach only; no unilateral cancellation within the first 18 months otherwise.
- Discounts & revenue recognition: finance to apply standard ASC guidance; any carveouts must be pre-approved by finance.

Laura — please incorporate the above into the redline and confirm legal sign-off. Ava — confirm to the customer that we can proceed on this basis and request the PO. Rishi — ensure the deal is recorded with the conditional approval notes in HubSpot (link above).
